title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused-ops for rope/rotary + kv-batching + scheduling tweaks
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token latency and CPU/GPU memory overhead for long-context workloads by upgrading attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variants, fusing rotary/rope ops into the attention kernel to avoid extra elementwise kernels, and improving KV-cache continuous batching scheduling so that prefix reuse and tail latency SLOs both improve. This PR upgrades the attention implementation to opt into FlashAttentionV2 when supported on target GPUs, adds a fused rotary/rope path to eliminate a separate rotary kernel at generation time, and changes the KV cache scheduler to form smaller, more frequent batches for active streams while allowing larger background batches for cold streams. Changes include runtime feature flags, a compatibility shim for older kernels, microbench harness updates, and new perf regression tests. Checklist: 1) FlashAttentionV2 integration and runtime toggles, 2) Fused rope/rotary ops and unit tests, 3) KV-cache continuous batching scheduler heuristics and config, 4) End-to-end perf runs and CI benchmarks, 5) Backcompat shim for models compiled with previous kernels, 6) Docs/console notes for rollout. Performance summary: on A100 80GB with fp16 we see median per-token generation latency improvements of 8-12% for base models at 2k context and 15-20% at 8k context for greedy decode, plus 10-15% reduction in overall GPU memory footprint when fused ops are enabled. Continuous batching changes reduce 95th percentile latency by ~25% for interactive workloads in internal canary. Rollout plan: default to new kernels for nightly/Dedicated pools, hold on Hosted until canary results are stable and telemetry shows no quality regressions. Related: ENG-2024 implements the scheduler heuristics, ENG-2078 tracks the fused-op correctness testcases. Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative about enabling fusion on older driver stacks; a runtime capability check gates the path.
